The six states that decide whether a TestFlight user's first bad day is survivable. Tokens from doc 12. Interactive: Omelette project `Macros Tracker Native setup`, option **7h** — one phone, arrows to step through all six.

**One rule governs all of them: never a dead end, and never lose the user's work.** Every screen has a way forward that does not depend on the thing that failed.

_[image omitted — see the Linear doc]_

## Shared layout

They are the same screen with different content, so build one component:

* A 40px accent rule, tinted by tone
* Mono tag naming the state
* Headline at 29px/800 — a sentence, not a label
* Body at 15px, one short paragraph
* Primary action filled in the tone colour, optional secondary as plain text

Tones: accent cyan for neutral, over-target orange for something the user needs to act on, fiber violet for informational, dim grey for transient.

## 1 · Camera access denied — orange

> **The camera is switched off for this app.**
> You can still log from your photo library, which works fine for anything you already photographed. If you want the in-app camera back, it is one switch in iOS Settings.

`OPEN SETTINGS` · *Use my library instead*

The library alternative is offered **before** the trip to Settings. Permission denial is not a broken app — it removes one of two equal entry points, and per doc 06 the library was always first-class.

## 2 · Estimate failed — orange

> **That did not come back.**
> The photo is saved and nothing is lost. You can try the estimate again, or enter the numbers yourself and move on — the entry does not need the model to exist.

`TRY AGAIN` · *Enter numbers manually*

A failed AI call must never cost the user their photo or block the log. Manual entry is the escape hatch and it must be reachable from the failure itself, not from somewhere else.

## 3 · Offline, entries queued — violet

> **Logged locally. It will catch up.**
> Gym wifi is bad wifi. Your photos and descriptions are held on the device and analysed the moment you have a connection — nothing needs your attention.

`DONE` · *See what is queued*

**The only one of the six that needs new backend thinking.** Everything else is copy and routing over what already exists. This needs a local queue, a retry policy, and a decision about what a queued entry looks like in the day list before its macros exist. Recommend designing it properly before TestFlight — this is where a bad first day comes from.

## 4 · Monthly AI limit reached — orange

> **300 analyses in the last 30 days. That is the ceiling.**
> Your oldest estimates age out over the next few days and the allowance comes back with them. Until then you can log entries by typing the numbers, and everything else — targets and history — works exactly as before.

`LOG WITHOUT AI` · *Why there is a limit*

Doc 09 requires a clear message rather than a silent failure. Note what the copy does: it names what still works. A quota screen that only says "you are out" reads as the app being broken.

**Rewritten 29 Aug 2026 for a rolling window.** The quota used to be a monthly counter reset on the 1st, and the copy said so. It is now a count of the user's calls over the last 30 days (docs 02 and 09), so nothing resets and the allowance returns gradually. "Comes back on the 1st" would have been a sentence the app could not keep. The word "streaks" also went, since doc 21 cut them.

## 5 · Session expired — dim, blocking

> **Signing you back in.**
> Nothing was lost. If this takes more than a moment you will land on the welcome screen and can sign in again.

`SIGN IN`

The visible half of the global 401 handler from doc 04: one silent refresh attempt first, and only if that fails does this appear. Most users should never see it.

## ~~6 · Targets timed out — green~~ — cut 31 Aug 2026

**Nothing to time out.** Target generation lost its AI call and is now one arithmetic pass on the server, so this state is unreachable.

It was a good screen and its reasoning outlives it. A brand-new user must never be stranded before they reach the home screen, and this was the one failure that could do it. That worry is what put an outside service in the first-run flow under review, and the answer was to take the service out rather than to design around it.

**Keep the tone for E4.** The photo estimate does call a model, it can time out, and this green treatment is the shape that failure should take: say what you have, say it is fine, offer the retry, never block.

The original copy:

> **We have your numbers anyway.**
> The judgement call did not come back in time, so these are straight from the formula — 2,180 calories, 176g protein, 32g fiber. They are sound. You can adjust them now or any time later.

`USE THESE TARGETS` · *Try the AI pass again*

## Cut: first run with nothing logged

A seventh state — "nothing logged ever" — was designed and removed. The home screen already teaches the loop, and a separate screen means a second layout for something each user sees once.

The narrower real problem: on day one the ring reads `2150 KCAL LEFT` at 100%, visually identical to a perfect day, and zeroed tiles read as broken. Handle it as a home-screen variant (ring centre `NOTHING LOGGED YET`, track only; tiles show `—`; one line of orientation where the entry list would be). See doc 16. **Not yet built.**

## Copy rules for all six

* Headline is a sentence a person would say. Never `Error`, never `Oops`
* Say what still works before saying what failed
* No exclamation marks, no apology theatre
* Never blame the network, the model, or the user
* Every state names the next action, and that action must not require the failed dependency

## Also undesigned

Sign in with Apple cancelled or unavailable, the reset-confirm screen from the emailed link, R2 upload failure specifically (distinct from the analyze failure above), and the day-list appearance of a queued entry.
